claim_one_line: THE GRAMMAR-LEVEL CONTROL: ACCESS TO THE McKAY GROUP IS GENERIC ACROSS THE METALLIC FAMILY. P0: a census of GRAMMARS (metallic words R^m L^m and their mod-N shadows in SL(2,Z/N)), not of manifolds -- the population the owner identified as the right one. WHY THIS CONTROL AND NOT B995-S: the chain DERIVES m004 (C1 Morse-Hedlund, C2 self-selection, C6 Thurston/Riley) and never selected it from a census, so B993-s finding that a third of manifolds also surject onto 2T DOES NOT BREAK THE CHAIN -- what it does is narrower and sharper, REMOVING THE ENDPOINT-S POWER TO CONFIRM THE BEGINNING, since reaching E6 is not evidence C1-C5 were right if a third of entry points reach E6 too; THE CHAIN CAN BE SOUND AND THE SM STILL FAIL TO CORROBORATE IT. C2 is a THEOREM WITH A UNIQUE FIXED POINT so the population at C1-C2 is SIZE ONE, and the relaxation is the metallic family R^m L^m for m >= 2, exactly what-if-C2-did-not-hold. COMPUTED: |SL(2,Z/N)| for N=2..9 is 6, 24, 48, 120, 144, 336, 384, 648, so |SL(2,Z/3)| = 24 = |2T| and N=3 IS THE ONLY MODULUS WHERE SL(2,Z/N) IS THE McKAY GROUP. The metallic shadows mod 3, i.e. the subgroup generated by R^m and L^m: m=1 gives 24, m=2 gives 24, m=3 gives 1, m=4 gives 24, m=5 gives 24, m=6 gives 1, m=7 gives 24 -- so FIVE OF SEVEN METALLIC WORDS GIVE THE FULL 2T, and only m divisible by 3 degenerate, trivially since R^m and L^m are then the identity. VERDICT: access to the McKay group, and therefore to E6, is GENERIC across the metallic family, shared by EVERY metallic word with 3 not dividing m, i.e. TWO THIRDS of the grammars. THE GRAMMAR-LEVEL CONTROL RETURNS THE SAME SHAPE AS THE MANIFOLD-LEVEL ONE (B993): the arrival at E6 does not distinguish the golden grammar, and the hypothesis that only m=1 reaches the McKay group is FALSE. SCOPE, a real limit stated rather than buried: this tests ONE route, the mod-3 shadow, which is the only modulus at which 2T can appear as a FULL SL(2,Z/N); L105-s discriminator is a DIFFERENT statement -- that the golden-s OWN CONDUCTOR is prime so its shadow IS the McKay group while the silver-s is a prime power (8) so the McKay partner sits ONE QUOTIENT DOWN -- which is about WHICH MODULUS IS THE WORD-S OWN, and this cell did NOT pin down that notion, computing the shadow at a fixed modulus instead. SO L105 IS NOT REFUTED HERE; what is refuted is the stronger and simpler hypothesis that access to 2T is itself grammar-specific, and the finer question -- whether the golden is the unique metallic word whose own conductor is 3 -- REMAINS OPEN as the surviving form of L146. Consistency check: at N=8 the golden generates all 384 of SL(2,Z/8) while the silver generates only 32, so the two DO differ at that modulus, compatible with L105 and showing the two statements are about different things.
